newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Fund and origin selling pushed robusta prices lower. Vietnam was cited as a major seller and some residual sales were also noted from Indonesia. January closed under psychological support at $1,400 per tonne, $27 lower at $1,397, while November finished $14 lower at $1,507. Some traders took the view that the London market ignored all bullish news and had traded on technical indicators. In New York the coffee market closed lower which might encourage some additional selling next week from technical traders. Fundamentally there has not been much change with physical premiums holding strong and ongoing talk of tight nearby supplies. Reports of further losses in the Costa Rican 1996/97 (October/September) crop had no impact on prices. A truck drivers strike entered its fifth day in Colombia, where a government minister was threatening to outlaw the action. December lost 80 points to close at 109.10 cents/lb, while March shed 95 points to close at 101.55 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 75 points and 1.60 cents/lb.

EL SALVADOR - El Salvador will lose 5 per cent of its estimated 1996/97 (October/September) coffee crop because of prolonged rains, Rene Martinez, manager of the Salvadoran Foundation for Coffee Investigation, said. He put the loss at around 123,000 60 kg bags of an estimated production of 2.2 million bags. He did not detail if rains had caused beans to fall from trees or whether the rains had damaged bean development in crucial flowering periods.

COLOMBIA - The Colombian government declared a strike by truck drivers illegal in a bid to end the five-day-old work stoppage that had shut down the country's export industries and dealt a serious blow to the economy. It was not immediately clear how the government would enforce the measure, however, since the tens of thousands of truck drivers are participating in the strike independently of the government and have no formal obligation to provide services to anyone. Olga Rosero Legarba, a leader of the independent Colombian Truckers Association, said the strike would continue 'indefinitely' despite the government move.

BRAZIL - Coffee stocks held by Brazilian cooperatives totalled 4.38 million 60.5 kg bags on September 30, the National Coffee Council (CNC) said, up from the 3.87 million bags held by cooperatives as of August 31 and also up from the 3.48 million bags held at the same stage last year when producers were bringing in the frost and drought-hit 1995/96 harvest.

UNITED KINGDOM - The UK imported 270,087 bags of coffee in July 1996, 3.4 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.777 million bags, nearly 13 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 18 per cent to 2.783 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Costa Rica (145,500 vs 202,800 bags), Colombia (166,600 vs 110,300 bags), Indonesia (146,500 vs 97,000 bags) and Vietnam (185,400 vs 74,100 bags). The country exported 336,300 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 5 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by nearly 20 per cent to 538,400 bags.
